kinds.deprecate_not_delete: a name leaves the library (or the reviewer asks to rename an existing one) with no deprecated alias: add one
kinds.deprecation_form: a deprecation exists but is wrong: theorem kept instead of alias, alias names the wrong old or new declaration, points at a deprecated one, changes the statement, or its message or location
kinds.should_it_go: is this retirement justified at all: keep both, do not deprecate, why was this removed or turned around, do it in its own PR
kinds.retire_redundant: the reviewer asks for a retirement the PR did not make: deprecate or remove a declaration as a duplicate or a special case of a general one
kinds.successor_fidelity: the moved, generated or replacing declaration lost or changed something the old one had: attributes, docstring, proof, layout, stale references
kinds.module_deprecation: deprecate the module or file, or split a file move from its deprecation
kinds.downstream_consequence: a retirement forces other changes, e.g. renames that relied on the removed namespace for dot notation

situations.removed_no_deprecation: the PR removes a public name and leaves no deprecation (structure: deleted_*, rename_no_alias)
situations.retired_with_deprecation: the PR retires a name with a deprecation: an alias for a removed declaration, or `@[deprecated]` on one it keeps (a modified target)
situations.name_survives: the name is still declared after the PR: moved, generated by an attribute, or not removed at all
situations.not_retired_by_pr: the declaration the ask is about is not retired by the PR; the reviewer proposes retiring it
situations.module: a file or module, not a declaration
